diagnosis.summary: Two concurrent faults are active: request rates to product-service and order-service have roughly tripled from their baselines, and payment-service p95 latency has risen from 110 ms to 1020 ms. Order-service is returning 5xx errors on 25% of requests and its p95 latency has risen from 130 ms to 1030 ms. The incident has been running for 4 minutes.
diagnosis.root_cause: A traffic surge across product-service and order-service, active at the same time as a payment-service p95 latency degradation, are the most likely concurrent root causes.
evidence: Product-service request rate rose from 15.0 rps to 44.8 rps, nearly a 3x increase from baseline.
Order-service request rate rose from 2.9 rps to 8.7 rps, also approximately 3x its baseline.
Payment-service p95 latency rose from 110 ms to 1020 ms, a 9.3x increase from baseline.
Order-service dependency error count rose from 0 to 150 per minute, where none were observed before.
Order-service 5xx error rate rose from 0.0 to 0.25, meaning 25% of requests are now failing.

Order-service p95 latency rose from 130 ms to 1030 ms, a 7.9x increase from baseline; payment-service p95 latency rose about 65 seconds before order-service errors appeared (observed sequence from correlated timestamps).
recommended_actions: Investigate payment-service Lambda logs and concurrency metrics immediately to identify what is holding p95 latency at 1020 ms, as order-service errors are tracking that degradation.

Check lambda_throttle_count on all services, since both product-service and order-service are running at roughly 3x their baseline request rates and all Lambda functions share account-level concurrency.
Apply or tighten API Gateway rate and burst limits on the affected stage to cap the traffic surge while the payment-service fault is being worked.
After stabilising payment-service, recheck order-service error_rate_5xx and dependency_error_count to confirm recovery before making further changes.

Record the onset times from the observed sequence when communicating with other teams: product-service traffic rose first at 17:03:00, payment-service latency rose at 17:04:05, and order-service errors appeared at 17:04:40.
